links.outcome: Effect of requiring verbatim supporting quote on coverage, accuracy, and verifiability of LLM classifications
links.effect: Quote requirement modestly reduced coverage (e.g., Gemini 98.3% to 92.8%); macro-F1 changed by model. Valid quotes in 83.3-91.2% of runs, but only 48.0-78.8% judged semantically supported.
links.quote: Mechanically valid quotes occurred in 83.3% to 91.2% of runs, yet only 48.0% to 78.8% of evidence-bearing predictions were judged semantically supported.

links.outcome: Validity and semantic support of quoted evidence in LLM outputs
links.effect: Mechanically valid quotes in 83.3% to 91.2% of runs, but only 48.0% to 78.8% of evidence-bearing predictions were judged semantically supported.
links.quote: Mechanically valid quotes occurred in 83.3% to 91.2% of runs, yet only 48.0% to 78.8% of evidence-bearing predictions were judged semantically supported.

links.outcome: Label reproducibility across three repeated runs per abstract
links.effect: Fleiss' kappa across repetitions ranged 0.829 to 0.969, indicating stable labels.
links.quote: Labels were stable across repetitions (Fleiss’ kappa 0.829 to 0.969).

unlisted_practices: Mechanically checkable verbatim quote requirement with exact-substring validation as automated audit trail
Restricting automation to semantically supported predictions (selective automation) trading coverage for precision
Allowing LLM abstention when information is insufficient

screen.practice: verbatim evidence quotation and automated verification guardrail
screen.reason: Empirical study testing whether enforcing a verbatim evidence quote requirement ('show your work') acts as an effective guardrail/audit mechanism for LLMs classifying clinical trial eligibility.
